rationale: The StepDownOnRemoval experiment executed in a clean copy (b973d91f2e78491f8305db97ba30499c, completed, exit 0) with all three comparisons complete and satisfied: the removed leader stepped down, a remaining voter was elected with the clock running, and the group committed a payload afterwards. This update interprets that receipt, records the authority transition as durable knowledge, and marks the question answered.

knowledge.statement: With StepDownOnRemoval enabled, removing the leader from the configuration produced the documented authority transition in the retained three-node scenario. A follower proposed the removal (index 41), after which node 1 was a StateFollower with voter false and no leader known (index 42: stepped_down true); with the clock advanced, node 2 became the new leader while nodes 1 and 3 were followers (index 43: new_leader 2); and a payload proposed on node 2 returned with no error and was committed, observed on nodes 2 and 3 only (index 45), consistent with the removed node no longer being part of the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process with StepDownOnRemoval true, ElectionTick 10 and HeartbeatTick 1; simple ConfChange removing node 1 proposed by node 2; ticks delivered in rounds of one with delivery between rounds until a leader emerged; reliable delivery.

interpretations.rationale: Admission: a follower proposed the removal of the sitting leader (index 41). Results: the removed leader left leadership rather than continuing to lead a configuration it is no longer part of, reported as StateFollower with voter false and no leader (index 42, stepped_down true); with the clock advanced in rounds, node 2 reported StateLeader while the other two reported StateFollower, so a new leader was elected among the remaining voters (index 43, new_leader 2, not equal to zero); and a proposal made on that leader returned with no error and was committed, observed on nodes 2 and 3 but not on the removed node 1 (index 45), which matches the new configuration. All three comparisons are complete and satisfied. No defect is claimed; the transition behaved as the option documents, and it complements the other scenarios in which the option is off and a removed leader keeps leading. The observation also confirms the boundary of the parent investigation's harm: the removed node remains a follower that applies nothing new, which is different from the re-admitted member case.

knowledge.assertion: the removed leader stepped down, a remaining voter was elected, and the group committed afterwards

counterevidence: The election needed the clock to be advanced because elections are tick driven; the observation depends on the harness supplying clock progress.

Only one removal direction was executed (a follower removing the leader); a leader proposing its own removal while a leadership transfer is in progress was not exercised, which the source notes is a different path.
Reliable delivery and no partitions, so nothing about a removed leader that cannot hear the new configuration is claimed.
limitations: One scenario instance with three nodes and a single removal; no claim about repeated removals or larger groups.

The payload's presence on nodes 2 and 3 only is consistent with the new configuration, but the run does not assert anything about the removed node's future participation beyond its state and membership at the recorded indices.
No defect judgment: the documented transition held in this scenario.
